# An `open` whose `commodity_scu:` is quoted.
#
# Every other value on an `open` block is quoted — `code:`, `description:`,
# `guid:`, `commodity.mnemonic:` — so quoting this one is an ordinary slip,
# and the setter behind it is a C `int` that refuses a string outright.
#
# What made it worse than a refusal: the account's `guid:` is claimed before
# the unit is set, and a claimed guid is in the book's collection whether or
# not the account was ever attached. So the refusal left the guid taken, and
# the pass that retried the same directive reported a collision with an
# account the book does not contain — naming a guid rather than the line that
# is actually wrong.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal about the unit, on both import paths.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_an_open_that_fails_after_it_is_attached.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 open Assets
	guid: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa0001"
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Fuel
	guid: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa0003"
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: "1000"
